# Exposing Blindspots: Cultural Bias Evaluation in Generative Image Models

> Paper by Huichan Seo*, Sieun Choi*, Minki Hong*, Yi Zhou, Junseo Kim, Lukman Ismaila, Naome Etori, Mehul Agarwal, Zhixuan Liu, Jihie Kim, Jean Oh
> Institutions: Carnegie Mellon University, Dongguk University, Delft University of Technology, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, University of Minnesota Twin Cities
> arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.20042
> Project Page: https://seochan99.github.io/ECB/
> Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/seochan99/ecb-datasets

## Summary

This paper presents a unified, reproducible cultural bias evaluation spanning six countries (US, India, Japan, Korea, Nigeria, Mexico), eight categories, and 36 subcategories with era-aware prompts. It audits both text-to-image (T2I) generation and image-to-image (I2I) editing, combining automatic measures, a culture-aware metric (retrieval-augmented VQA), and expert human judgments from country-native reviewers.

## Key Findings

- **Global-North defaults**: Country-agnostic prompts converge to U.S.-centric, modern aesthetics even with controlled schema and era cues, flattening cross-country distinctions.
- **Metric-human gap**: CLIPScore and aesthetic metrics remain stable while the culture-aware signal and native raters flag rapid semantic drift during iterative editing.
- **Shortcut editing**: Iterative I2I edits substitute palette shifts and flags for genuine cultural attributes, often retaining source identity for Global-South targets.
- **Demographic skew**: Gender-neutral occupation prompts surface male dominance and light skin tones across all models tested.

## Culture-Aware Metric

A retrieval-augmented VQA metric that integrates Wikipedia-derived cultural knowledge via FAISS retrieval with Qwen2 models. Achieves 74% agreement with native reviewers on best selections and 84% on worst selections.

## Evaluation Protocol

- **Countries**: United States, India, Japan, Korea, Nigeria, Mexico
- **Schema**: 8 categories, 36 subcategories
- **Eras**: Traditional, Modern, Era-agnostic prompts
- **T2I Models**: FLUX.1-dev, Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large, DALL-E 3
- **I2I Models**: FLUX.1-dev, Step1X-Edit
- **I2I Studies**: Multi-loop editing (5 iterations), Attribute addition, Cross-country restyling
- **Human evaluation**: Country-native expert reviewers via custom web platform

## Three I2I Editing Studies

1. **Multi-loop editing**: Five successive cultural instructions cause outputs to collapse to homogenized wedding aesthetics regardless of target locale.
2. **Attribute addition**: Stepwise attribute additions reveal weak text rendering and brittle handling of culture-specific details.
3. **Cross-country restyling**: Models rely on superficial palette swaps while leaving Global-South identities largely unchanged.

## Released Assets

- Complete image corpus from both T2I and I2I studies
- All prompts with era-aware variants
- Model execution configurations
- Human evaluation survey platform
- Culture-aware metric implementation
